correctness.rationale: Intersections of two row-column crosses have only row, column or diagonal-pair forms; further intersections produce singletons or empty, proving the complete normal form and count. All closed sets are generated by singleton atoms; pairwise joins recover rook adjacency except in the thin case, where closure factorizes into two height-two factors. Four-corner and three-matching witnesses establish arity lower bounds; explicit row/column saturation plus matching-triple rules establish upper bounds. Standalone exhaustive checks agree on parameter cases, but are not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The theorem exactly classifies all concepts and reveals when the unlabeled lattice reconstructs both rook coordinates versus forgets the matching of column positions. Thin boards acquire independent within-row permutations (wreath-product symmetry) rather than ordinary rook-graph symmetries. On thick boards the optimal one-shot Horn premise width jumps from the iterative optimum of three to four, with explicit sharp witnesses and constructive bases. These are structural and inference-theoretic invariants of a natural infinite family, not merely an isolated count.
